memory_verse.label: Memory Verse
memory_verse.text: “Because there is one bread, we who are many are one body, for we all partake of the one bread.” (1 Corinthians 10:17)

devotion.label: Insight / Reflection
devotion.text:
The Lord’s Supper is not merely a personal spiritual experience; it is a foundational pillar of the Church.
The one bread proclaims that Christ is one, and that all of us who are united in Him are one body. When we partake of the Lord’s Table, we do not receive Christ alone, we also receive one another in love.
The breaking of the bread reminds us that Christ was broken and crushed on the cross. At the same time, it is a call for our selfishness, pride, and divisions to be broken. A life that refuses to deny itself cannot reveal the true meaning of the broken bread.
Those who partake of the one bread cannot live divided, isolated, or without unity. The Lord’s Supper moves us from a self-centered “I” to a united “we.”
The Church is not a gathering of empty individuals sitting together; it is the divine body, energized and activated by the life of Christ Himself. Participating in the Lord’s Supper is a call to remain in a holy life. As we partake of Christ’s body, we must also embrace His character. He gave Himself to protect us. He laid down His life to give us life. Likewise, we are called to give our lives to deny ourselves, to love, and to forgive.
The Lord’s Supper asks us a searching question:
I eat the bread that represents His body, but do I love His true body, the Church?. Communion begins at the altar, but it must be revealed in daily life. Just as the bread is one, love, sacrifice, and unity must also be one, both in the Church and in our personal lives.

quote.label: Today's Quote
quote.text: “The Lord’s Supper unites us not only with Christ, but also with one another.” — John Stott

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, as we partake of the one bread, train us to live as one body. Remove divisions and hardened hearts from among us. Amen.

conclusion.label: A Word to You
text: Every time you partake of the Lord’s Table, you are entering into communion with Christ. Through the breaking of the bread, God calls you to live as a witness revealing unity and oneness of heart.

recommended_book.label: Recommended Book
recommended_book.title: Knowing Scripture
recommended_book.author: R. C. Sproul
recommended_book.quote: God teaches invisible spiritual truths through visible, doctrinal signs. The breaking of the bread reveals both the sacrifice of Christ and the unity of the Church.
